entries.declaration_header:
def moment (v k : ℝ) : ℕ → ℝ

human_reorganization: Lemma 3.1 gives a general finite spectral/coordinate proof of the specific verified Jacobi realizations, including a zero last pivot. It is a classical human reconstruction, not a newly named Lean theorem.
The Gram/Schur-complement proof reorganizes the formal completed-square and witness proofs without changing their parameter criteria.
The rational example v=1,k=1/2 and the scale normalization are direct human corollaries of the exact criteria; the formal open-gap module uses a different rational example.
The proof of boundary cross-moment nonvanishing uses monotonicity of a quadratic on [0,1/5] to simplify the formal inequalities.

The separate target (1,0,2,4,12,32,89) is not identified with a Gaussian-cubic parameter. Its cubic Gram form is positive semidefinite but the preceding quadratic block is singular, outside the earlier Jacobi lemma hypothesis.

The explicit two-atom positions 1 plus/minus sqrt(3) and weights are a printed human coordinate realization of the actual formal two-dimensional coordinate-zero spectral law; its mean and null recurrence identify the same law.

The native index n+1 is renamed N>=1. The remote atom has weight N^-6 and exact sixth-moment contribution one. Actual probability vectors approach nonrepresentable data although their laws converge on all bounded observables.

The quantitative total-variation bound 2N^-6, uniform tightness via the sixth-moment bound and lower-power uniform tail estimate are explicitly proved classical deductions. The formal source directly supplies bounded-observable convergence, exact moment limits, uniform sixth-moment bound and failure of uniform sixth-tail control.

Nonclosedness concerns the actual moment image on unbounded support, not the positive-semidefinite matrix cone or loss of probability mass. Coordinate multiplication fails on the null quotient even though the semidefinite quotient norm itself exists.

The pure-order functional with formal generating series exp(a z^p), integer p>=2, has a fully reconstructed polynomial Stein identity and unique moment recurrence. For p>2 and a nonzero, the literal square (x-p!a x^(p-1))^2 has value -2(p!a)^2. The two separate null squares therefore cannot be quotiented as an additive null space. Positivity holds exactly for a=0 or p=2 and a>=0, with actual centered Gaussian realization; strict positivity holds exactly for p=2 and a>0. The classical Gaussian integration-by-parts proof and all low-degree conventions are explicit. This all-degree theorem is confined to the pure-order functional, and does not promote the mixed Gaussian-cubic finite tests to an all-degree classification. The broader Marcinkiewicz obstruction is credited only as primary historical context, not imported through a formal exponential as a characteristic function.
